runs.goal_hypothesis: Test whether a long, heuristic-heavy original regimen can retain broad heuristic competence through 10.24M steps.

results_insights.insight: The terminal worst-side win rate remained only 1%, revealing a severe robustness floor.
The agent was strong as X against the offensive heuristic.
The same checkpoint was almost unable to win as O against the defensive heuristic.

reasoning: The heuristic-heavy schedule learned strong performance in favorable policy/side matchups but not balanced robustness.
The 1% defensive-O result likely drives the 1% worst-win-rate floor despite 92% offensive-X performance.
Evaluation uses 100 games per side, but stochastic training and the multi-stage schedule prevent attributing the imbalance to one knob.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Continue from 21 snapshots and double the nominal horizon to test whether extended self-play preserves heuristic skill.

results_insights.insight: The latest logged checkpoint had a zero-win matchup.
Offensive-X fell from the predecessor's 92% to 36% at the comparable logged step.
The generic heuristic X matchup remained relatively strong but below the predecessor's 94%.

reasoning: Extended continuation produced clear forgetting in the formerly strong offensive-X matchup.
Snapshot-pool continuation likely shifted the training distribution away from preserving heuristic competence.
Although MLflow status is complete, metrics stop at step 10.24M despite total_timesteps=20.48M, so conclusions apply to the latest observed checkpoint and logging/horizon semantics are a caveat.
